title: Vancomycin enriches Parabacteroides goldsteinii in the gut and promotes reconstruction of the hepatobiliary system in cholestasis.
abstract: Impaired bile secretion disrupts the gut microbiome and perpetuates cholestatic liver injury. Vancomycin (VCM) has been shown to improve cholestasis in human patients, but its biological effects remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic effects of VCM on microbiome modulation and the restoration of liver function. VCM was administered in a modified Abcb11 knockout (KO) mice model with pre-existing cholestasis to examine its therapeutic effects and microbiome changes. After 2 weeks of treatment, VCM significantly decreased serum bilirubin while maintaining stable transaminase in the KO mice. Three-dimensional imaging of pan-CK expression by immunofluorescence revealed improvement of the disrupted biliary epithelium and interconnected bile duct network, as evidenced by increased coverage and cumulative duct length in the liver. Gene expression and hepatic bile acid profiling demonstrated that VCM enhanced canalicular/sinusoidal bile acid export while repressing bile acid synthesis, with a reduction in tauro-β-muricholic acid, the predominant bile acid in mice, in KO livers. Fecal microbial analysis using next-generation sequencing identified Parabacteroides goldsteinii (PG) as the predominant species after VCM treatment. KO mice fed PG demonstrated improved cholestasis, with significantly reduced direct bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, total bile acids in serum, as well as fewer reactive ductules in the liver. In vitro culture of ductal organoids suggested that PG directly promoted the growth of cholangiocytes. RNA sequencing results suggested that PG suppressed pro-inflammatory Lyz1 (mouse orthologous gene of human LYZ) and Aqp4 and increased pro-proliferative Muc6 and Chrm3. This study highlights the therapeutic potential of VCM in cholestasis by enriching PG in the gut and improving biliary structures in the liver, identifying PG as a potential probiotic with beneficial effects in cholestasis. © 2026 The Pathological Society of Great Britain and Ireland.
authors: Hsu SH, Chua HH, Liou BY, Cheng YY, Lin CR, Chen YH, Yang TH, Wu SH, Tsuei DJ, Chen HL, Chang MH, Ni YH, Chen HL.
screening_reason: Examines gut microbiome manipulation by vancomycin and specific gut bacterial species in cholestatic liver injury.
summary_ja: 本研究は、バンコマイシン（VCM）投与が胆汁停滞モデルマウスの腸内細菌叢と肝胆道系再構築に与える影響を解析した。VCM処理により、血清ビリルビン値が低下し、三次元画像解析において胆管ネットワークの損傷が改善した。細菌叢解析の結果、VCM投与後に Parabacteroides goldsteinii（PG）が優勢種として同定され、PG単独の投与によっても胆汁停滞や肝臓の傷害が軽減された。さらに、PGは胆管オルガノイドの成長を直接促進し、炎症性遺伝子の抑制と増殖関連遺伝子の発現増加を引き起こした。
summary_en: This study investigated how vancomycin treatment alleviates cholestatic liver injury in a mouse model. Vancomycin treatment enriched Parabacteroides goldsteinii in the gut, which reduced serum bilirubin and promoted the reconstruction of disrupted biliary structures. Administration of P. goldsteinii alone improved cholestasis and directly stimulated cholangiocyte proliferation in vitro.
key_finding_ja: バンコマイシン投与によって増殖する腸内細菌 Parabacteroides goldsteinii が、胆汁停滞マウスの胆管構造の再構築と肝機能改善を促進した。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸内細菌 P. goldsteinii の同定は、胆汁停滞性肝疾患に対する腸内細菌叢を標的としたプロバイオティクス治療法に期待をもたせる。

title: Probiotic Clostridium butyricum CB-a alleviates intestinal inflammation through targeted modulation of the microbiome metabolome axis.
abstract: This study investigated the capacity of Clostridium butyricum CB-a, a novel environmental isolate with unique ecological adaptability, to restore host-microbiome homeostasis in a dextran sodium sulfate (DSS)-induced murine model of intestinal dysbiosis. Integrated 16S rRNA gene sequencing and untargeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics revealed that CB-a (1 × 10⁸ CFU/mL, administered orally) fundamentally restructured the colonic microbial architecture. Specifically, it enriched beneficial, short-chain fatty acid (SCFA)-producing consortia (e.g., Lactobacillus , Bacteroides , and Alloprevotella ) while suppressing opportunistic pathobionts ( Escherichia-Shigella ) and mitigating excessive mucin-degrading bacteria ( Akkermansia ). This ecological shift was accompanied by a pronounced metabolic reconfiguration, highlighted by the significant restoration of fecal SCFA pools, predominantly butyrate ( P C. butyricum in functional interventions targeting microbiota-associated inflammatory disruptions.IMPORTANCESevere gut inflammation, such as inflammatory bowel disease, is often driven by a breakdown in our natural gut bacteria. Although probiotics are popular treatments, how they actually repair the gut remains largely unknown. Our study highlights the remarkable healing ability of Clostridium butyricum CB-a, a natural bacterium isolated from the environment. We discovered that this microbe acts as an ecological engineer for the digestive system. It actively rescues the damaged gut by promoting the growth of beneficial bacteria and suppressing harmful ones. This positive shift triggers the release of natural, healing molecules that calm the immune system and rebuild the protective gut lining. By uncovering the exact steps this bacterium takes to restore digestive harmony, our work provides a powerful blueprint for designing highly targeted, natural probiotic therapies to combat severe intestinal diseases.
authors: Liu J, Yue H, Li J, Fang Z, Bi T, Li C, Yi H, Zhao Y, Feng Y, Zhao S, Hu Y.
screening_reason: Investigates how probiotic gut bacteria restore host-microbiome homeostasis and metabolite production in intestinal inflammation.
summary_ja: 本研究では、デキストラン硫酸ナトリウム（DSS）誘発腸管ディスバイオーシス動物モデルを用いて、プロバイオティクス菌株 Clostridium butyricum CB-a の治療効果を検証した。CB-a の経口投与により、短鎖脂肪酸産生菌が増加し、病原性細菌や過剰なムチン分解菌が抑制されるなど、結腸の細菌叢構造が再編された。この変化に伴い、糞便中の酪酸をはじめとする短鎖脂肪酸濃度が顕著に回復し、トリプトファン代謝産物の増加も観察された。さらに、腸管上皮バリア機能の改善や炎症性サイトカインの抑制、抗炎症性サイトカインの増加が確認された。
summary_en: This study evaluated the therapeutic potential of Clostridium butyricum CB-a in a dextran sodium sulfate-induced mouse model of intestinal dysbiosis. Oral administration of CB-a restructured the colonic microbiome by enriching short-chain fatty acid producers and suppressing pathobionts. This microbial shift restored short-chain fatty acid levels, repaired the gut barrier, and attenuated intestinal inflammation.
key_finding_ja: Clostridium butyricum CB-a の投与は、腸内細菌叢の再構築と短鎖脂肪酸代謝の回復を通じて腸管炎症を抑制しバリア機能を修復した。
why_it_matters_ja: 環境由来の特定プロバイオティクスを用いた代謝・細菌叢の制御手法は、炎症性腸疾患に対する新たな治療戦略の開発に貢献する可能性がある。

title: Nutritional and environmental determinants of maturation and disruption of the early life gut microbiome: A narrative review.
abstract: The first 1000 days of life represent a critical window for gut microbiome assembly, with lifelong implications for child growth, immune development, and disease risk. This review synthesizes evidence on maternal, perinatal, and especially nutritional factors that influence early-life intestinal colonization and highlights the consequences of microbial disruptions during this period. In utero exposures and birth-associated factors can profoundly shape microbial development, reducing diversity and beneficial taxa. Nutrition exerts a particularly dominant and modifiable influence: breastfeeding supports Bifidobacterium-rich communities, while formula use and early complementary feeding shape microbiota diversity and metabolic function. Dietary quality, fiber intake, and food diversity are key determinants of microbial maturation and resilience. Undernutrition and inadequate diets contribute to microbial dysbiosis, creating a self-reinforcing cycle of malabsorption, growth failure, and long-term metabolic consequences. Early microbial perturbations are associated with a range of acute and chronic diseases, including necrotizing enterocolitis, obesity, type 1 diabetes, inflammatory bowel disease, and atopic disorders. Strategies to restore microbial balance require further validation, particularly in nutritionally vulnerable populations. The absence of a universal definition for a "healthy" pediatric microbiome limits the development of targeted interventions. Emerging metrics, such as microbiota-for-age z-scores and functional microbiome profiling, may help define microbiota maturity and therapeutic efficacy.
authors: Burow C, Shenderey R, Chowdhury F, Shah N, Pai N.
journal: JPEN. Journal of parenteral and enteral nutrition
screening_reason: Focuses directly on the establishment, maturation, and disruption of the early-life gut microbiome.
summary_ja: 本総説は、生後1000日間における腸内細菌叢の定着と成熟に影響を与える母体、周産期、および栄養要因に関する知見をまとめている。母乳育児や食事の質、食物繊維の摂取は微生物の成熟と耐性維持を支援する一方で、不適切な食事や栄養失調はディスバイオーシスを引き起こす。初期の細菌叢の乱れは、壊死性腸炎、肥満、1型糖尿病、炎症性腸疾患などの発症リスク増加に関連している。著者らは、小児細菌叢の成熟度や治療効果を評価するための新たな評価指標の必要性を指摘している。
summary_en: This review synthesizes evidence on nutritional and environmental factors shaping the gut microbiome during the first 1000 days of life. Breastfeeding, dietary diversity, and fiber intake support microbial maturation, whereas nutritional inadequacies can lead to dysbiosis and long-term health risks. Early microbial disruptions are associated with conditions like necrotizing enterocolitis, obesity, and inflammatory bowel disease, underscoring the need for validated metrics to assess microbiome health.
key_finding_ja: 生後初期の栄養や環境要因が腸内細菌叢の成熟を規定し、その乱れは将来の多様な疾患リスクと関連している。
why_it_matters_ja: 小児における腸内細菌叢の健全な定着メカニズムの理解は、栄養介入による疾患予防戦略の策定に役立つ可能性がある。

title: Neuropsychiatric disorders and gut dysbiosis: what is the real impact of the kynurenine pathway?
abstract: The human gut microbiome (GM) influences host physiology through the production of bioactive metabolites. Increasing evidence links GM dysbiosis to neuropsychiatric disorders (NPDs), including anxiety disorders, major depressive disorder (MDD), bipolar disorder (BD), and schizophrenia (SCZ), via bidirectional signaling along the gut-brain axis (GBA). Among the pathways connecting gut and brain, the tryptophan-kynurenine pathway (TKP) has emerged as a central inflammatory and neuromodulatory mechanism. During immune activation and dysbiosis, tryptophan metabolism shifts toward kynurenine production, generating metabolites with distinct biological effects. Kynurenic acid (KYNA) exerts neuroprotective actions through NMDA receptor antagonism and reduced oxidative stress, whereas quinolinic acid (QUIN) and 3-hydroxykynurenine (3-HK) promote excitotoxicity, mitochondrial dysfunction, and neurodegeneration. Altered KYNA/QUIN balance appears to represent a transdiagnostic feature across NPDs, with preferential QUIN accumulation in mood disorders and pathological KYNA elevation in SCZ, suggesting potential therapeutic relevance. In parallel, the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR), activated by tryptophan-derived microbial metabolites, regulates intestinal barrier integrity, immune responses, and neuroimmunometabolic signaling, functioning as a molecular link between the GM, immune system, and brain. This review explores the interactions among GM dysbiosis, TKP alterations, mitochondrial dysfunction, and AhR signaling in anxiety disorders, MDD, BD, and SCZ, highlighting their potential as biomarkers and targets for personalized therapies.
authors: Reyes-Martínez S, Zapata-Martín Del Campo CM, Tesoro-Cruz E, Baldi S, Aguirre-García MM, Amedei A.
screening_reason: Focuses on the gut microbiome, tryptophan-kynurenine microbial metabolism, and the gut-brain axis in neuropsychiatric disorders.
summary_ja: 本総説は、不安症、大うつ病性障害、双極性障害、統合失調症などの神経精神疾患における腸内細菌叢の乱れとキヌレニン経路の役割を概括している。トリプトファン代謝がキヌレニン生成へシフトすることで、神経保護作用を持つキヌレン酸と神経毒性を持つキノリン酸などのバランスが変化する。さらに、微生物由来代謝物によって活性化されるアリル炭化水素受容体（AhR）が腸管バリア機能や免疫応答、神経代謝シグナルを調節することが解説されている。これらの相互作用は、診断用バイオマーカーや個別化治療の標的として期待されている。
summary_en: This review outlines the role of gut dysbiosis and the tryptophan-kynurenine pathway in neuropsychiatric disorders, including anxiety, depression, bipolar disorder, and schizophrenia. Alterations in tryptophan metabolism change the balance between neuroprotective kynurenic acid and neurotoxic metabolites such as quinolinic acid. The review also highlights how aryl hydrocarbon receptor signaling connects gut microbiota, immune regulation, and brain function, presenting potential biomarker and therapeutic targets.
key_finding_ja: 精神疾患においてキヌレニン経路の代謝物バランスの変動やAhRシグナルが腸内細菌叢、免疫系、脳のクロストークを媒介している。
why_it_matters_ja: キヌレニン経路やAhRシグナル伝達の解明は、神経精神疾患に対する新たなバイオマーカー開発や個別化治療法の確立につながる可能性がある。

title: LKB1 functions as a checkpoint for neuronal-glial balance during enteric nervous system development.
abstract: How the energy status of enteric progenitors controls neurogliogenesis and the subsequent formation of the complex enteric nervous system (ENS) remains poorly understood. We previously showed that the tumor suppressor kinase LKB1 is essential for postnatal ENS maintenance through amino acid homeostasis. Here, we investigated LKB1's functions during embryonic ENS formation using a genetically engineered mouse model with conditional Lkb1 inactivation in neural crest progenitors during gut colonization. Using advanced 3D imaging techniques on cleared tissue including light sheet microscopy and adaptive optics confocal microscopy, we found that Lkb1 loss impairs early neuronal differentiation followed by progressive glial degeneration, leading to hypoganglionosis and compromised digestive tissue integrity. Notably, Lkb1 inactivation induced a transient upregulation of the glial stress marker S100β during gestation, suggestive of a reactive glial state preceding glial loss. Consistent with this response, Lkb1 loss elevated oxidative stress in the digestive tract and in neural crest progenitors and their glial derivatives, triggering DNA damage and p53 activation. Although p53 ablation rescued glial specification in vitro and glial maintenance in vivo, it only partially restored ENS architecture in vivo without rescuing enteric neuron numbers. Together, these findings establish LKB1 as a critical metabolic checkpoint governing neuronal-glial balance during ENS development and suggest that dysregulated LKB1 signaling may contribute to human enteric neurogliopathies.
authors: Lucas A, Appaix F, Allard J, Mével-Aliset M, Radu AG, Fauvelle F, Favier B, Grichine A, Maurer J, Hainaut P, Attardi L, Billaud M, Torch S, Thibert C.
screening_reason: Directly addresses the mechanisms governing embryonic enteric nervous system development, neurogliogenesis, and enteric neural crest progenitors.
summary_ja: 本研究では、発生期における腸管神経系（ENS）の神経・グリアバランスに対する腫瘍抑制因子LKB1の役割をマウスモデルを用いて解析した。神経生殖細胞におけるLkb1の欠損は、初期の神経分化障害とそれに続く進行性のグリア変性を引き起こし、低神経節症を呈することが明らかになった。また、Lkb1欠損により酸化ストレスおよびp53活性化が誘導され、p53の欠損はグリアの維持を一部回復させたものの、神経元数の減少は改善しなかった。これにより、LKB1はENS発生における神経・グリアの均衡を制御する重要な代謝チェックポイントであることが示された。
summary_en: This study examined the role of LKB1 in maintaining the neuronal-glial balance during enteric nervous system (ENS) development using conditional knockout mouse models. Loss of Lkb1 impaired early neuronal differentiation and led to progressive glial degeneration, oxidative stress, and p53 activation. Although p53 deletion restored glial maintenance, it failed to fully rescue enteric neuron numbers, establishing LKB1 as a key metabolic checkpoint in ENS development.
key_finding_ja: LKB1は発生期の腸管神経系において酸化ストレスやp53応答を制御し、神経・グリアのバランスを決定する代謝チェックポイントとして機能することが明らかになった。
why_it_matters_ja: LKB1シグナルの異常がヒトの腸管神経グリア病変に関与している可能性を示唆しており、発生学的な治療標的の理解に寄与する可能性がある。

title: Distinct enteric nervous system pattern in obstructed defecation syndrome and slow-transit constipation: a controlled digital pathology study.
abstract: Purpose Chronic constipation comprises heterogeneous clinical entities, including slow-transit constipation (STC) and functional defecation disorders such as obstructed defecation syndrome (ODS). Although neuroenteric mechanisms are implicated, reproducible histomorphological correlates remain incompletely defined, partly due to methodological heterogeneity and lack of standardized quantification. The study characterizes the myenteric plexus morphology and neuroimmune cell distribution across clinically defined subgroups of functional bowel disorders using a standardized digital pathology approach. Methods Retrospective observational cohort study at a tertiary colorectal referral center. A total of 100 patients after bowel surgery were included: ODS (n = 17), STC (n = 24), combined ODS + STC (n = 28), and a control cohort without clinically evident bowel motility disorders (n = 31). Digital morphometric assessment of ganglionic density and morphology, neuronal content (immunohistochemistry against MAP2, HuC/D), and the distribution of CD3-positive T-lymphocytes within and around myenteric ganglia were performed. Results Ganglionic density differed significantly between groups (p = 0.002), with increased density in ODS, whereas STC values were comparable to controls. Neuronal content per ganglion was preserved across all groups as demonstrated by MAP2 and HuC/D analyses. In contrast, the presence of CD3-positive lymphocytes was reduced in all constipation groups, most pronounced in STC, affecting both the intra- and periganglionic compartments. Conclusion Functional bowel motility and defecation disorders appear to show distinct neuroarchitectural and neuroimmune patterns. Increased ganglionic density in ODS contrasts with preserved neuronal content and reduced presence of T-lymphocytes, particularly in STC. These findings represent associations rather than proven disease mechanisms, derived from comparison with a surgical rather than a healthy control cohort. Standardized digital morphometry nonetheless provides a reproducible framework for phenotypic characterization of chronic constipation and may support future studies linking enteric structure to function. Trial registration Clinicaltrials.gov (NCT05016700; 09/12/2020).
authors: Bedau T, Mirzaie-Kuzehgarani A, Madukkakzhy J, Halbe L, Quaas A, Rudroff C.
screening_reason: Directly characterizes enteric nervous system morphology, myenteric plexus neuroarchitecture, and neuroimmune cell distribution in motility disorders.
summary_ja: 本研究は、閉塞性排便症候群（ODS）および徐通過性便秘症（STC）の患者における筋層内神経叢の形態と神経免疫細胞の分布をデジタル病理手法を用いて評価した。100例の腸管手術患者（ODS、STC、ODS+STC、および対照群）を対象に、神経叢の密度、神経元含有量、およびCD3陽性Tリンパ球の分布を解析した。その結果、ODS群では神経節密度の増加が認められた一方、STC群を含む便秘群全般で筋層内神経叢周囲および神経節内のCD3陽性Tリンパ球の減少が観察された。これらの知見は、機能性腸管運動障害において特異的な神経構造および神経免疫パターンが存在することを示している。
summary_en: This retrospective cohort study used standardized digital morphometry to analyze myenteric plexus morphology and neuroimmune cell distribution in patients with obstructed defecation syndrome (ODS) and slow-transit constipation (STC). Patients with ODS exhibited increased ganglionic density, whereas neuronal content per ganglion remained preserved across all groups. Additionally, CD3-positive T-lymphocytes were reduced in constipation groups, most prominently in STC. These results suggest distinct neuroarchitectural and neuroimmune alterations associated with specific functional constipation phenotypes.
key_finding_ja: 閉塞性排便症候群では筋層内神経節密度の増加が認められる一方、徐通過性便秘症を含む便秘患者群では神経節周辺および内部のCD3陽性Tリンパ球が減少していることが明らかになった。
why_it_matters_ja: これらの知見は健常者ではなく手術対照群との比較による関連性を示すにとどまるものの、便秘の病態解明や分類に向けたデジタル病理評価の有用性を示す可能性がある。

title: Gut bacteria regulate intestinal motor circuits by metabolizing sex hormones.
screening_reason: Directly investigates how gut bacteria and their metabolism of sex hormones regulate intestinal motor circuits.
summary_ja: 本研究は、腸内細菌が性ホルモンを代謝することによって腸管運動回路を調節するメカニズムを検討したものである。腸内微生物群集が宿主の生体分子変換を通じて消化管機能をどのように制御するかについて示している。性ステロイド代謝と腸管神経系・運動性の相互作用に関する新たな知見を提供する。
summary_en: This study investigates how gut bacteria regulate intestinal motor circuits by metabolizing sex hormones. The findings highlight the interaction between microbial hormone metabolism and intestinal motility regulation.
key_finding_ja: 腸内細菌が性ホルモンを代謝することで、腸管の運動回路を調節することが示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸内細菌叢によるホルモン代謝が腸管運動に与える影響の解明は、性差を考慮した消化器疾患の病態理解につながる可能性がある。

title: The Dual Roles of Microglia- and Astrocyte-Derived Exosomes in Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury: from Intercellular Communication to Therapeutic Prospects.
abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) is a complex pathological process characterized by metabolic dysfunction, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and structural and functional alterations of the neurovascular unit (NVU). Across different studies, CIRI has been reported to be associated, to varying degrees, with neuronal injury and neurological dysfunction. Increasing evidence suggests that exosomes (EXOs) derived from glial cells, particularly microglia and astrocytes, play critical roles in mediating intercellular communication and regulating injury progression in CIRI. This review systematically summarizes the context-dependent and heterogeneous functions of glia-derived EXOs in CIRI. Microglia-derived EXOs exhibit diverse and context-dependent functions depending on the activation state of donor cells and the surrounding microenvironmental conditions. Under pro-inflammatory conditions, EXOs released from microglia may exacerbate inflammation by carrying cargo components such as circular RNAs (circRNAs) and pro-inflammatory proteins, whereas EXOs associated with reparative states may support tissue recovery through the delivery of functional non-coding RNAs. These cargo components may participate in pathological regulation through multiple signaling pathways. Among them, the nuclear receptor coactivator 4 (NCOA4) axis is associated with ferroptosis, ubiquitin-specific protease 14 (USP14) with proteostasis/apoptosis, and thioredoxin-interacting protein (TXNIP) with inflammasome activity, all of which have been linked to reduced neuronal injury and functional recovery. In addition, M2-type-derived EXOs may participate in the regulation of synaptic plasticity and axonal regeneration by modulating the plexin A2 (PLXNA2)/RhoA/ROCK2 signaling pathway. Astrocyte-derived EXOs (ATC-EXOs) further contribute to NVU regulation. A2-type-derived EXOs have been reported in multiple experimental models to be associated with reduced NLR family pyrin domain containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome activity and alterations in the PI3K/Akt and MAPK signaling pathways, accompanied by attenuated inflammatory responses and improved blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity in these models. Some studies suggest that these effects may be related to the transition of microglial phenotypes toward reparative states; however, sufficient in vivo mechanistic evidence supporting their direct regulatory effects remains lacking. In contrast, neurotoxic astrocytes (A1)-derived EXOs exhibit limited or context-dependent effects. Importantly, exosome function is highly state-dependent and cannot be fully explained by simplified pro-inflammatory microglia anti-inflammatory microglia (M1/M2) or A1/A2 paradigms. Moreover, extracellular vesicle heterogeneity and methodological limitations remain major challenges. Despite promising therapeutic potential, including the ability to cross the BBB and enable multi-target regulation, significant barriers to clinical translation persist, such as delivery efficiency, biodistribution, and standardization. Overall, glia-derived EXOs represent a dynamic and multi-level regulatory system in CIRI and a promising platform for precision therapeutic strategies.
authors: Yang Z, Chen H, Zhang Z, Wei X, Han W, Peng T, Zhu D, Liu C.
screening_reason: Reviews microglial and astrocytic extracellular vesicles in mediating neuroinflammation and neurovascular unit signaling during cerebral ischemia.
summary_ja: 脳虚血再灌流障害（CIRI）において、ミクログリアやアストロサイトなどのグリア細胞由来エクソソーム（EXO）が細胞間コミュニケーションにおいて二面的な役割を果たすことがレビューされています。炎症状態のミクログリア由来EXOは炎症反応を悪化させる一方、修復状態のEXOやA2型アストロサイト由来EXOは神経保護や血液脳関門の保護に寄与します。また、NCOA4軸やUSP14、TXNIPなどのシグナル系がEXOの内包物によって調節されることが示されています。しかし、実験モデルの不均一性や評価手法の限界から、臨床応用には送達効率や標準化などの課題が存在します。
summary_en: This review summarizes the dual, context-dependent roles of microglia- and astrocyte-derived exosomes in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. Pro-inflammatory glial exosomes can exacerbate neuroinflammation, whereas reparative phenotypes release exosomes that attenuate inflammasome activity and preserve blood-brain barrier integrity. Translational challenges such as vesicle heterogeneity, targeting efficiency, and standardization are also critically addressed.
key_finding_ja: グリア細胞由来エクソソームは、ドナー細胞の活性化状態に応じて脳虚血再灌流障害を悪化または改善する二面的な調節機構を持つことが体系化された。
why_it_matters_ja: グリア細胞由来エクソソームの精密な分子機構理解と標準化は、脳卒中に対する精密医療や新規ドラッグデリバリーシステムの開発に寄与する可能性があります。

title: Recent insights in pathogenesis of endometriosis with focus on gut microbiota.
abstract: EMs is a chronic, estrogen-dependent systemic inflammatory disorder defined by the ectopic implantation of endometrial glands and stroma and is frequently associated with dysmenorrhea, chronic pelvic pain, infertility, and substantial impairment in quality of life. Despite its high prevalence and socioeconomic burden, the etiopathogenesis of EMs remains incompletely elucidated and appears to involve intricate interactions among endocrine dysregulation, immune dysfunction, epigenetic reprogramming, ferroptosis, miRNA-mediated gene regulation, environmental exposures, and lifestyle-related factors. Accumulating evidence has increasingly implicated GM dysbiosis in EMs development and progression. Alterations in microbial diversity and composition have been associated with changes in host immune homeostasis, estrogen metabolism, intestinal barrier integrity, inflammatory signaling cascades, microbial-derived metabolites, and gut-brain axis communication, which may foster a pro-inflammatory pelvic microenvironment that in turn may facilitate lesion implantation, angiogenesis, neuroinflammation, and pain sensitization. Elevated lipopolysaccharide levels, reduced short-chain fatty acid production, Th17/Treg imbalance, macrophage polarization, and epigenetic modulation have also been associated with GM perturbations in EMs. This review synthesizes current advances in understanding the multifactorial mechanisms underlying EMs pathogenesis, with a particular emphasis on microbiota-host interactions. We also discuss emerging microbiota-targeted therapeutic strategies, including probiotics, dietary modulation, and fecal microbiota transplantation, highlighting their translational potential as adjunctive approaches for disease management and personalized medicine in EMs.
authors: Kardan R, Hemmati J, Nazari M, Chegini Z, Ansariniya H.
screening_reason: Focuses on the central role of gut microbiota dysbiosis, microbial metabolites, and gut-brain interactions in endometriosis pathogenesis.
summary_ja: 子宮内膜症（EMs）は異物性の内膜組織が増殖する全身性慢性炎症性疾患であり、その病態には多様な因子が関与しています。近年の研究では、腸内細菌叢の多様性や組成の変化（ディスバイオーシス）が子宮内膜症の発症や進展に関連していることが示されています。腸内細菌叢の異常は、エストロゲン代謝や腸管バリア機能、LPS上昇や短鎖脂肪酸減少を介して骨盤内のプロ炎症性環境を維持し、神経炎症や痛みの増幅に寄与すると考えられています。本レビューでは、腸内細菌と宿主の相互作用メカニズムを整理し、プロバイオティクスや食事療法などの細菌叢ターゲット療法の可能性を論じています。
summary_en: This review synthesizes the multifactorial pathogenesis of endometriosis, with a focus on the key roles played by gut microbiota dysbiosis. Alterations in intestinal microbial composition disrupt host immune homeostasis and estrogen metabolism, facilitating a pro-inflammatory pelvic microenvironment, neuroinflammation, and pain sensitization. Emerging microbiota-targeted interventions such as probiotics and dietary modulation are discussed as novel adjunctive strategies.
key_finding_ja: 腸内細菌叢のディスバイオーシスが、エストロゲン代謝や免疫応答の変更を通じて子宮内膜症の病態形成や神経炎症、痛み増幅に関与していることが総括された。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸内細菌叢を標的とした介入は、子宮内膜症に対する補助的治療や個別化医療の確立に貢献する可能性があります。

title: Microglial 5-LOX-activating protein antagonism alleviates leukotriene-driven neuroinflammation.
abstract: In multiple sclerosis (MS), the chronic, unresolved nature of neuroinflammation within the central nervous system (CNS) remains a major obstacle for effective therapeutic intervention. This challenge arises primarily due to an incomplete understanding of the dysregulated inflammatory and pro-resolving pathways underlying MS lesion progression. Bioactive lipid mediators (LMs), biosynthesized through the coordinated actions of specific enzymes like lipoxygenases (LOX) and cyclooxygenases (COX), are key regulators of both the initiation and resolution of an inflammatory response; however, their spatial organization and functional role during MS pathology have not been fully elucidated. Here, by using pneumatically assisted nanospray desorption electrospray ionization (PA nano-DESI) mass spectrometry imaging and immunohistochemistry, we reveal an increase in the LM leukotriene B 4 (LTB 4 ) in human MS white matter compared to controls, with further enrichment in MS lesions relative to perilesional areas, alongside elevated microglial 5-LOX activating protein (FLAP) expression. Pharmacological antagonism of FLAP suppresses LTB 4 biosynthesis in human-induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived microglia with only marginal effects on the microglia transcriptional phenotype as determined by RNA sequencing. Moreover, in vivo FLAP antagonism ameliorates disease severity and spinal cord inflammatory gene expression in the experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) model, an animal model of MS, in both a prophylactic and therapeutic settings. This coincided with reduced local LTB 4 biosynthesis and reduced levels of inflammatory monocytes within the spinal cord during EAE. Together these findings establish the FLAP/LTB 4 axis as a driver of neuroinflammation and a druggable therapeutic target for chronic inflammatory CNS disorders like MS.
authors: Konings J, Mingneau F, Chornyi S, Hansen CE, van der Brugt RTM, van Elk TG, Bolkaerts L, Batens B, Tóth G, Lanekoff I, Vaz FM, Cardilli A, Sels M, van der Pol SMA, de Vries HE, Giera M, Werz O, Kessels S, Verberk SGS, Bogie JFJ, Rijnsburger M, Hendriks JJA, Kooij G.
screening_reason: Focuses on microglial FLAP-driven leukotriene biosynthesis as a key neuroinflammatory pathway in multiple sclerosis models.
summary_ja: 多発性硬化症（MS）における持続的な神経炎症の制御には、脂質メディエーターの動態やその合成経路の解明が重要である。本研究は、ヒトMS患者の白質病変部およびヒトiPSC由来ミクログリアを用いて、5-リポキシゲナーゼ活性化タンパク質（FLAP）とロイコトリエンB4（LTB4）の役割を解析した。その結果、MS病変部ではFLAPの発現とLTB4レベルが亢進しており、FLAP拮抗薬の投与によりLTB4生合成が抑制された。さらに、EAEマウスモデルにおいてFLAP拮抗は脊髄における炎症性遺伝子発現や炎症性単球の浸潤を抑え、病勢を改善した。
summary_en: The study evaluated the role of the FLAP/LTB4 axis in neuroinflammation associated with multiple sclerosis using human brain tissue, iPSC-derived microglia, and an EAE mouse model. The authors observed elevated LTB4 levels and microglial FLAP expression in human MS lesions compared to non-disease controls. Pharmacological antagonism of FLAP effectively suppressed LTB4 biosynthesis and reduced clinical severity and spinal cord inflammation in EAE mice.
key_finding_ja: FLAP/LTB4軸の阻害は、ヒトiPSC由来ミクログリアおよびEAEモデルにおいてロイコトリエン生合成と神経炎症を抑制する。
why_it_matters_ja: ロイコトリエン経路を標的としたFLAP拮抗薬が、多発性硬化症などの慢性神経炎症性疾患に対する標的治療につながる可能性を示している。

title: New insights on microglial lysosomal acidification: A therapeutic target of neurodegenerative diseases.
abstract: Background Microglia, the resident immune cells of the central nervous system (CNS), maintain brain homeostasis and respond to pathological insults. Microglial dysfunction has been implicated in the pathogenesis of several neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and multiple sclerosis. Impaired lysosomal function, particularly defective lysosomal acidification, leads to the accumulation of undegraded material, thereby promoting neuroinflammation and neuronal damage. Purpose This review examines the mechanisms governing lysosomal acidification in microglia and evaluates its potential as both a therapeutic target and a prognostic biomarker in neurodegenerative diseases. Methods The literature on microglial lysosomal acidification, lysosomal pH regulation, autophagy, and neurodegeneration was searched in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science. Relevant mechanistic, preclinical, and translational studies were critically appraised and synthesized. Results Lysosomal acidification is increasingly recognized as a key regulator of microglial function and homeostasis. Defective acidification, driven by dysregulation of the vacuolar H+-ATPase (V-ATPase) proton pump, TFEB/TFE3 signaling pathways, and lysosomal ion channels such as TRPML1 and TMEM175, impairs autophagic flux and substrate degradation, facilitating the accumulation of neurotoxic aggregates including amyloid-β and α-synuclein. Emerging evidence suggests that the degree of microglial lysosomal acidification may serve as a prognostic biomarker for disease progression and therapeutic response. Restoration or enhancement of lysosomal acidification through pharmacological modulation of lysosomal pH, activation of autophagy, or targeting of key regulatory pathways has been shown to re-establish microglial homeostasis, attenuate neuroinflammation, and confer neuroprotection in preclinical models. Conclusion Restoration of microglial lysosomal acidification represents a promising therapeutic strategy for neurodegenerative diseases. A deeper understanding of the molecular mechanisms regulating lysosomal acidification in microglia may facilitate the identification of novel biomarkers and therapeutic targets, ultimately contributing to the development of innovative interventions for neurodegenerative disorders.
authors: Jaganathan R, Vijayakumar S, Chen Y, Ye J, Bakthavatchalam P, Wankar D, Yang C, Iyaswamy A, Li M.
screening_reason: Examines microglial lysosomal function and its direct role in regulating neuroinflammation in neurodegenerative diseases.
summary_ja: ミクログリアのライソゾーム酸化機能は、中枢神経系の恒常性維持や神経変性疾患の病態に重要な役割を果たしています。V-ATPaseやTFEB/TFE3、TRPML1などの調節障害による酸化異常は、オートファジーを低下させ、アミロイドβやαシヌクレインなどの有害タンパク質凝集体の蓄積を促進します。本レビューでは、ミクログリアのライソゾームpH調節機構と、その異常が神経炎症や神経細胞障害へ及ぼす影響を整理しています。さらに、ライソゾーム酸化の回復を狙った薬物投与やオートファジー活性化が、前臨床モデルにおいて神経保護効果を示したことを報告しています。
summary_en: This review examines the molecular mechanisms governing microglial lysosomal acidification and its dysregulation in neurodegenerative diseases. Defective acidification driven by impaired V-ATPase and ion channel signaling leads to autophagic dysfunction and the accumulation of neurotoxic protein aggregates. Pharmacological restoration of microglial lysosomal pH attenuates neuroinflammation and confers neuroprotection in preclinical models.
key_finding_ja: ミクログリアのライソゾーム酸化障害は有害タンパク質凝集体の蓄積と神経炎症を促進し、その酸化機能の回復が前臨床モデルで神経保護効果を示すことが示された。
why_it_matters_ja: ミクログリアのライソゾームpH調節機構の解明は、神経変性疾患に対する新たなバイオマーカーや治療ターゲットの開発につながる可能性があります。

title: Neuron-specific suppression of aberrantly active Toll-NFκB signalling mitigates pathogenic tau hyperphosphorylation via Gsk-3β in Drosophila.
abstract: Chronic brain ailments like Alzheimer's disease and Frontotemporal dementia, together referred to as tauopathies, are strongly influenced by neuroinflammation, an age-associated functional anomaly. Neuroinflammation arising from a dysfunctional innate immune response, such as Toll-NFκB signalling, is implicated in modulating tau pathophysiology, with limited understanding of the molecular mechanisms. Pathogenic hyperphosphorylation of tau and its aggregation into neurotoxic species is considered as a central trigger of tau pathology; however, the mechanistic association between these pathogenic events and the Toll signalling remains largely unexplored. We examined the status of the Toll signalling in Drosophila tauopathy models and evaluated whether its modulation modifies disease severity. We present compelling evidence that neuronal expression of pathogenic human tau causes aberrant activation of the Toll signalling. In line, its additional upregulation further aggravates disease severity, while genetic downregulation of Toll components remarkably alleviates both structural and functional deficits. We subsequently noted that knockdown of the Toll pathway attenuates pathogenic tau hyperphosphorylation in a site-specific manner, largely coinciding with restoration of physiological activity of Gsk-3β/Akt/PP2Ac signalling, a relatively less explored molecular axis in neurons. Our study posits a potential contribution of neuron-intrinsic altered Toll signalling cascade in tau pathogenesis, warranting further exploration of this evolutionarily conserved pathway as a therapeutic target.
authors: Aggarwal P, Sarkar S.
journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
screening_reason: Investigates neuronal Toll-NFκB neuroinflammatory signaling and its role in modulating tau hyperphosphorylation.
summary_ja: 本研究は、ショウジョウバエのタウオパチーモデルを用いて、神経細胞におけるToll-NFκBシグナル伝達と病理的タウ過リン酸化の関連を調査した。病理学的人体タウの神経発現によりTollシグナルが異常活性化され、このシグナルをノックダウンすることで構造的・機能的欠損が軽減された。さらに、Toll経路の抑制はGsk-3β/Akt/PP2Acシグナル系の正常な活性を回復させ、特定部位におけるタウの過リン酸化を著しく抑制した。以上の結果は、神経細胞自律的な自然免疫シグナルの異常がタウ病態に関与していることを示している。
summary_en: This study examined the role of Toll-NFκB innate immune signaling in Drosophila models of tauopathy. Neuronal expression of pathogenic human tau induced aberrant Toll activation, whereas genetically suppressing Toll components rescued structural and functional deficits. Knockdown of this pathway attenuated site-specific tau hyperphosphorylation by restoring Gsk-3β/Akt/PP2Ac signaling balance.
key_finding_ja: ショウジョウバエモデルにおいて、神経細胞のToll-NFκBシグナル抑制がGsk-3β活性を介してタウの過リン酸化と病理的障害を軽減した。
why_it_matters_ja: 神経細胞内の固有な免疫シグナル経路とタウ病態のメカニズム解明は、アルツハイマー病などのタウオパチーに対する新たな分子標的治療薬の開発に繋がる可能性がある。

title: Lycium barbarum glycopeptide attenuates ischaemic stroke by inhibiting inflammation via SIRT3-mediated NLRP3 deacetylation.
abstract: Background Inflammatory processes play a critical role in ischaemic stroke. Acetylation of NLRP3 is a key step in amplifying neuroinflammation.(LbGP), a bioactive glycoprotein derived from Lycium barbarum, has anti-inflammatory potential, but its mechanisms in post-stroke neuroinflammation remain unclear. Aim This study aimed to investigate the efficacy and molecular mechanisms of LbGP in alleviating neuroinflammation following ischaemic stroke. Methods A mouse model of middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO)/reperfusion was used to induce focal cerebral ischaemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury. Microglial cells were subjected to oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation. Neurological recovery was assessed by Y-maze and open-field tests. Molecular mechanisms were explored using Western blotting, ELISA, co-immunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence. Results LbGP significantly reduced cerebral infarct volume, attenuated neuroinflammation and improved functional recovery in I/R mice. Mechanistically, LbGP suppressed NLRP3 inflammasome activation through Sirtuin 3-mediated inhibition of NLRP3 acetylation, a finding further validated by exacerbated neuroinflammation in Sirt3-knockout mice. Conclusion This study demonstrates for the first time that LbGP alleviates post-stroke neuroinflammation via Sirt3-mediated deacetylation of NLRP3, thereby disrupting inflammasome activation, and identifies LbGP as a promising therapeutic candidate for ischaemic stroke.
authors: Han B, Ma C, Zhang L, Meng S, Bai M, Yu Z, Duan M, Liu J, Guo J, Shi C, He M, Liu Y.
screening_reason: Examines post-stroke neuroinflammation and the mechanistic regulation of NLRP3 post-translational deacetylation by SIRT3.
summary_ja: クコ多糖糖ペプチド（LbGP）は虚血性脳卒中における抗炎症作用を有することが示唆されているが、その詳細な分子機構は不明であった。本研究では、脳虚血再灌流障害マウスモデルおよび酸素糖剥奪/再酸素化微小膠細胞を用いて、LbGPの治療効果と機序を検証した。実験の結果、LbGPの投与は脳梗塞領域を減少させ、神経炎症の抑制および行動機能の回復を促進した。メカニズムとして、LbGPはSIRT3を介したNLRP3の脱アセチル化を誘導し、NLRP3インフラマソームの活性化を抑制することが明らかになった。
summary_en: This study investigated the therapeutic potential and molecular mechanisms of Lycium barbarum glycopeptide (LbGP) in ischemic stroke using mouse and cell models. The authors demonstrated that LbGP treatment significantly reduced cerebral infarction volume, attenuated neuroinflammation, and improved functional recovery following ischemia/reperfusion injury. Mechanistically, LbGP inhibited NLRP3 inflammasome activation by promoting SIRT3-mediated deacetylation of NLRP3.
key_finding_ja: LbGPはSIRT3を介したNLRP3の脱アセチル化を促進することで、インフラマソーム活性化および虚血後の神経炎症を抑制する。
why_it_matters_ja: タンパク質のアセチル化修飾の調節を介した神経炎症抑制アプローチが、虚血性脳卒中に対する新たな治療選択肢となる可能性が期待される。

title: Citrullination in proteins of the polycomb repressor complex 1.
abstract: The Polycomb repressive complexes can be considered a paradigm of chromatin-based gene regulation in animals. Two of the proteins involved in such complexes are the Ring finger protein 1 (RING1) and the intrinsically disordered protein RING1A and YY1 binding protein (RYBP), which binds to RING1 in some of the Polycomb complexes. Peptidyl arginine iminohydrolases (PADIs) are enzymes involved in the post-translational modification of arginine to citrulline. PADI4, one of the five isoforms of PADI in humans, citrullinates RING1B and RYBP at specific arginines at their C-terminal (Arg231) and N-terminal (Arg53) regions, respectively. In this work, we studied in vitro and in silico whether isolated peptides from each protein, encompassing those wild-type arginines and their citrulline-modified counterparts, were capable of binding to PADI4. The isolated peptides, either in wild-type or modified form, were monomeric and disordered as indicated by far-UV CD and NMR. The affinity constants of peptides for PADI4, as measured by fluorescence, biolayer interferometry (BLI) and isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC), were in the low micromolar range (dissociation constants around 10-20 μM), and the affinities were smaller for the citrullinated variants. Molecular docking simulations showed that the isolated peptides from each protein, either in wild-type form or modified variants, targeted the active site of PADI4, corresponding to the catalytic residue Cys645. These findings suggest that the isolated peptides were capable of binding to the enzyme with affinities similar to those of intact RING1B or RYBP, and that citrullination of the arginines diminished the affinity for the enzyme.
authors: Álvarez-Rodríguez MG, Capone E, Vega S, Rejas V, Rizzuti B, Velazquez-Campoy A, Neira JL.
screening_reason: Focuses on mechanistic biochemical characterization of peptidyl arginine deimination (citrullination), a post-translational protein modification.
summary_ja: 本研究は、Polycomb抑制複合体1（PRC1）の構成タンパク質であるRING1BおよびRYBPに対するPADI4によるシトルリン化修飾とその相互作用を解析した。野生型およびシトルリン化修飾を受けたペプチドを用いたインビトロおよびインシリコ解析により、両ペプチドがPADI4の活性部位にマイクロモルレベルの親和性で結合することが示された。シトルリン化修飾によりPADI4に対する結合親和性は低下することが各種分光学的および熱力学解析から明らかになった。これらの結果は、ペプチド単体でもPRC1構成成分とPADI4との相互作用特性を反映していることを示している。
summary_en: This study evaluated the in vitro and in silico binding of wild-type and citrullinated peptides from RING1B and RYBP to the peptidyl arginine deiminase enzyme PADI4. Both forms of isolated peptides bound to the active site of PADI4 with low micromolar affinity, with citrullination resulting in reduced binding affinity. These findings demonstrate that isolated peptide fragments preserve binding characteristics similar to intact proteins while undergoing citrullination-induced affinity changes.
key_finding_ja: PADI4によるRING1BおよびRYBPのシトルリン化修飾は、酵素に対する基質ペプチドの結合親和性を低下させることがインビトロおよびインシリコ解析で示された。
why_it_matters_ja: クロマチン調節複合体タンパク質の翻訳後修飾メカニズムの解明は、エピジェネティックな遺伝子発現制御の理解を深めるのに役立つ可能性がある。

title: SARS-CoV-2 Spike Peptides Trigger Nociceptive Responses Through Spinal TLR4 Pathways.
abstract: Background Pain is a common neurological manifestation of COVID-19, yet the mechanisms by which SARS-CoV-2 spike protein fragments contribute to nociceptive processing remain poorly understood. We investigated whether spike-derived peptides directly activate spinal neuroimmune pathways involved in pain signalling. Methods Male C57BL/6 mice received intrathecal administration of three synthetic SARS-CoV-2 spike-derived peptides (PSPD2001, PSPD2002 or PSPD2003) or saline. Mechanical nociception was assessed using the von Frey test. The involvement of spinal Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), microglia and p38 MAPK/NF-κB signalling was investigated using pharmacological antagonists, TLR4 knockout mice, RT-qPCR, ELISA, immunofluorescence, CX3CR1 GFP/+ mice, human C20 microglial cells and molecular dynamics simulations. Results All spike-derived peptides induced mechanical nociception, with PSPD2003 producing the most pronounced response. PSPD2003 increased spinal TLR4 expression, elevated TNF-α and IL-6 levels and promoted activation of dorsal horn microglia, demonstrated by increased TMEM119- and CX3CR1-positive cells. These nociceptive and neuroinflammatory effects were abolished by pharmacological inhibition of TLR4, microglia, p38 MAPK and NF-κB signalling, as well as in TLR4 -/- mice, demonstrating that TLR4 signalling is essential for PSPD2003-induced pain. PSPD2003 also induced a hypertrophic phenotype in human microglial cells, while molecular dynamics simulations supported a stable interaction with the TLR4/MD-2 complex. Conclusions These findings identify a previously unrecognized neuroimmune mechanism whereby a SARS-CoV-2 spike-derived peptide triggers spinal nociception through TLR4-dependent microglial activation and downstream p38 MAPK/NF-κB signalling, highlighting the spinal TLR4-microglia axis as a potential therapeutic target for COVID-19-associated and post-viral pain. Significance statement This study provides the first evidence that SARS-CoV-2 spike-derived peptides directly activate a spinal TLR4-dependent neuroimmune pathway to induce nociception. By integrating behavioural, pharmacological, genetic, cellular and computational approaches, it identifies microglial activation and p38 MAPK/NF-κB signalling as key mechanisms linking viral peptides to pain, providing a mechanistic framework for COVID-19- and post-viral pain and supporting TLR4 as a potential therapeutic target.
authors: Silva BE, Cardoso RR, Rosário LMR, Prado JP, Dos Santos RS, Veras FP, de Souza M, Cilli EM, Olivier D, de Andrade Belo MA, Charlie-Silva I, Caixeta ES, Barchuk AR, Nunes-Silva A, Romero TRL, Galdino G.
screening_reason: Demonstrates a spinal neuroimmune pathway where microglial activation and TLR4 signaling mediate viral peptide-induced nociception.
summary_ja: COVID-19における神経障害としての痛みの発症メカニズムを解明するため、SARS-CoV-2スパイク由来ペプチドの脊髄における作用をマウスおよび細胞モデルで検証しました。スパイクペプチド（特にPSPD2003）を髄腔内投与すると、マウスで機械的疼痛様反応が誘発されることが判明しました。このノシセプション反応は、脊髄後角におけるミクログリア活性化、TLR4発現上昇、およびp38 MAPK/NF-κBシグナルの増強を伴っていました。遺伝子欠損マウスや阻害剤を用いた実験により、これらの変化がTLR4依存的であることが証明されました。
summary_en: Intrathecal administration of a SARS-CoV-2 spike-derived peptide induced mechanical nociception in mice by triggering spinal microglial activation. This effect was mediated by TLR4 signaling and downstream p38 MAPK/NF-κB pathways. Genetic knockout or pharmacological inhibition of TLR4 or microglia completely abolished the peptide-induced pain response.
key_finding_ja: SARS-CoV-2スパイク由来ペプチドが脊髄のTLR4-ミクログリア軸およびp38 MAPK/NF-κBシグナルを介して機械的疼痛を惹起することが明らかになった。
why_it_matters_ja: 脊髄のTLR4-ミクログリア経路は、COVID-19関連疼痛や感染後痛に対する新たな治療標的となる可能性を示唆しています。

title: Isolation and characterization of seven phages infecting gut Bacteroides .
abstract: Despite the importance of the gut microbiota in human health, isolation and studies of phages infecting abundant gut bacteria have increased only in the past few years. The majority of phages isolated and characterized thus far infect facultative or strict aerobic bacteria. The aim of this study is to isolate and sequence new phages that infect Bacteroides species, which are abundant and prevalent members of the human gut microbiota across populations. Here, we report the isolation and genomes of seven phages infecting three human gut Bacteroides species from the United States. These phages are within the Caudoviricetes class and have siphovirus structural morphology. We observe a variable host range among five B. fragilis -infecting phages. This work provides resources to support further characterizations of gut-resident phages and their biology.
authors: Mundru K, Khatun K, Huang YY.
screening_reason: Focuses on isolating and characterizing phages that infect Bacteroides, key bacterial inhabitants of the human gut microbiome.
summary_ja: 本研究では、ヒトの腸内細菌叢において優勢なBacteroides属の3種に感染する7種の新規バクテリオファージを分離し、全ゲノム解析を行った。分離されたファージはCaudoviricetes綱のシフォウイルス形態を有し、B. fragilis感染ファージにおいて多様な宿主域を示すことが確認された。これにより、これまで好気性菌用ファージに偏っていた腸内ファージ研究に新たなリソースが追加された。本成果は、腸内嫌気性細菌とファージの相互作用や生態系における役割の解明に貢献する。
summary_en: Researchers isolated and characterized seven novel phages targeting three human gut Bacteroides species from individuals in the United States. These siphovirus-like phages within the Caudoviricetes class exhibited variable host ranges among Bacteroides fragilis-infecting isolates. This work expands available resources for studying phages that infect dominant anaerobic members of the human gut microbiota.
key_finding_ja: ヒト腸内で優勢なBacteroides属細菌に感染する新規のシフォウイルス科ファージ7種が分離・ゲノム解読され、宿主域の多様性が確認された。
why_it_matters_ja: 優勢な腸内偏性嫌気性細菌を標的とするファージリソースの拡充は、腸内マイクロバイオームの生態的制御機構の解明につながる可能性がある。

title: Therapeutic potential of spirulina and its bioactive compound phycocyanin in neuropsychiatric disorders.
abstract: Neuropsychiatric disorders are of great health concerns, and despite the availability of drugs, effective therapies are poor, emphasizing the need for novel therapeutics. Among the natural substances screened for neuromodulation properties, Spirulina platensis, a cyanobacterium, and its main bioactive compound (phycocyanin) have attracted great attention. Substantial evidence demonstrates that spirulina and phycocyanin possess neuroprotective properties by targeting multiple interconnected cellular and molecular pathways, including apoptosis, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and regulators of synaptic plasticity. Consequently, these compounds have shown therapeutic potential in experimental models of Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, multiple sclerosis, cerebral ischemia, epilepsy, schizophrenia, depression, and autism spectrum disorder. Herein, we summarize various cellular and molecular pathways which are affected by spirulina and phycocyanin in neuropsychiatric disorders.
authors: Talebi Taheri A, Motamedzadeh A, Zahedi E, Farasat A, Dadgostar E, Aschner M, Khanifar H, Rahmati-Dehkordi F, Tamtaji OR.
screening_reason: Evaluates therapeutic targeting of neuroinflammation and neuroprotective pathways in neuropsychiatric disorders.
summary_ja: 本総説は、スピルリナ（Spirulina platensis）およびその主要成分であるフィコシアニンの神経精神疾患における治療的可能性をまとめたものである。これらの化合物は、アポトーシス、酸化ストレス、神経炎症、シナプス可塑性調節因子などの分子経路に作用して神経保護効果を発揮する。アルツハイマー病、パーキンソン病、多発性硬化症、うつ病などの実験モデルでその有用性が報告されている。
summary_en: This review summarizes the therapeutic potential of Spirulina platensis and its bioactive compound phycocyanin in various neuropsychiatric disorders. These compounds exhibit neuroprotective effects by targeting multiple pathways including oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, apoptosis, and synaptic plasticity. Evidence from experimental models supports their application in conditions such as Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and depression.
key_finding_ja: スピルリナとフィコシアニンは神経炎症や酸化ストレスなどを標的とし、各種神経精神疾患の実験モデルで神経保護効果を示す。
why_it_matters_ja: 既存治療が不十分な神経精神疾患に対して、自然由来の神経保護化合物を用いた新たな治療選択肢の開発につながる可能性がある。

title: Protecting the gut microbiome when treating bloodstream infections: the price of anaerobic coverage.
authors: Kolodyazhna A, Wiersinga WJ.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Focuses directly on strategies for preserving the gut microbiome during antimicrobial treatment for bloodstream infections.
summary_ja: 本論文は、血流感染症の治療において嫌気性菌をカバーする抗菌薬投与が腸内細菌叢に与える影響や保護の重要性を論じたものである。提供された抄録には具体的な実験データや臨床パラメータの記載は含まれていない。感染症治療時の腸内細菌叢保護に伴う影響や課題に関する議論が展開されている。
summary_en: This paper discusses the impact of anaerobic antimicrobial coverage on protecting the gut microbiome during the treatment of bloodstream infections. No detailed experimental or clinical data were provided in the available text. The work highlights considerations regarding gut microbiome preservation in infectious disease management.
key_finding_ja: 血流感染症治療時の嫌気性菌カバーが腸内細菌叢に及ぼす影響と、細菌叢保護に関する治療上の重要性が議論されている。
why_it_matters_ja: 抗菌薬投与における腸内細菌叢の保護と感染制御のバランスを考慮した治療戦略の検討に寄与する可能性がある。

title: Caspase-1-mediated pyroptosis drives secondary thalamic neurodegeneration after focal cerebral infarction.
abstract: Background Secondary neurodegeneration in brain regions remote from the primary infarct contributes substantially to long-term neurological dysfunction after ischemic stroke. Although pyroptosis has been implicated in acute ischemic injury, its contribution to delayed secondary thalamic degeneration remains poorly understood. This study investigated whether canonical inflammasome-mediated pyroptosis contributes to secondary thalamic injury following focal cerebral infarction. Methods and results A permanent distal middle cerebral artery electrocoagulation model was established in male C57BL/6 mice. Adeno-associated virus-mediated short hairpin RNA targeting caspase-1 was stereotactically delivered into the ipsilateral thalamus two weeks before ischemic injury. Behavioral assessments, histological analyses, immunofluorescence, and Western blotting were performed at predefined time points after infarction. Focal cortical ischemia induced marked activation of caspase-1 and downstream pyroptotic signaling within the ipsilateral thalamus, accompanied by progressive neuronal loss, astrocytic activation, and microglial polarization toward a pro-inflammatory phenotype. Targeted caspase-1 knockdown significantly improved sensory and cognitive performance, preserved thalamic neurons, reduced astrocyte proliferation, suppressed the expression of gasdermin D, interleukin-1β, and interleukin-18, and promoted polarization of Iba-1-positive cells toward an anti-inflammatory M2-like phenotype. Conclusions Canonical inflammasome-mediated pyroptosis plays an important role in secondary thalamic neurodegeneration after focal cerebral infarction. Targeted inhibition of caspase-1 attenuated remote neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration, supporting canonical inflammasome signaling as a promising therapeutic target for limiting delayed brain injury following ischemic stroke.
authors: Sun W, He D, Wang S, Zhang H, Liu X, Zhang Y.
screening_reason: Investigates the role of canonical inflammasome activation, microglial polarization, and neuroinflammation in secondary thalamic neurodegeneration after cerebral infarction.
summary_ja: 局所性脳梗塞の後に生じる梗塞巣から離れた視床の二次性神経変性は、長期的な神経機能障害の原因となる。本研究では、マウス脳梗塞モデルを用いて、標準的インフラマソームを介したカスパーゼ-1依存性パイロトーシスが二次性視床障害に寄与するかを検討した。皮質虚血後、同側視床においてカスパーゼ-1の活性化とパイロトーシスシグナル、神経細胞死、炎症性変化が認められた。視床局所でのカスパーゼ-1ノックダウンは、パイロトーシス関連因子の発現を抑制し、ミクログリアの抗炎症性M2様フェノタイプへの偏向を促して感覚・認知機能を改善した。
summary_en: This study examined the role of canonical caspase-1-mediated pyroptosis in secondary thalamic degeneration following focal cerebral infarction in mice. Cortical ischemia induced marked activation of caspase-1 and downstream pyroptotic signaling in the ipsilateral thalamus, accompanied by progressive neuronal loss and neuroinflammation. Targeted knockdown of caspase-1 attenuated pyroptotic signaling, promoted M2-like microglial polarization, preserved thalamic neurons, and improved sensory and cognitive performance.
key_finding_ja: 局所性脳梗塞後の視床において、カスパーゼ-1依存性のパイロトーシスが二次的な神経変性と神経炎症を駆動している。
why_it_matters_ja: 脳梗塞後の遠隔部位で進行する二次性神経変性を抑制するための分子標的として、カスパーゼ-1シグナル伝達系が有望である可能性を示唆している。

title: Urolithin B Ameliorates Depressive-like Behavior and Hippocampal Neuronal Damage in Depressed Rats via regulation of the SLP2/PINK1/Parkin Signaling Pathway.
abstract: Background Depression is a highly prevalent mental disorder, with current medications often limited by delayed onset and insufficient efficacy, underscoring the urgent need to explore novel therapeutic strategies. Urolithin B (UB), a natural ellagitannin-derived metabolite, exhibits anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities in neuroinflammation, yet its role in depression remains unclear. Objective The present research aimed to uncover possible effects of UB on depressive-like behavior and hippocampal neuronal damage in a rat model of depression and to preliminarily elucidate its underlying molecular mechanisms. Methods A rat model of depression was created using the chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) paradigm, after which UB intervention was applied. To evaluate depressive-like behaviors, several behavioral tests were conducted, including sucrose preference test, forced swim test, tail suspension test, and open field test. Hippocampal pathological changes and related factor expression were evaluated using histopathology, immunofluorescence, and ELISA. Potential targets were screened via single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data obtained from the GEO database. Subsequently, the function of the identified target gene was validated through in vitro knockdown/overexpression experiments and an in vivo rescue experiment. Results UB significantly ameliorated depressive-like behaviors in CUMS rats and alleviated hippocampal neuronal damage, synaptic loss, and neuroinflammation. scRNA-seq analysis revealed a significant upregulation of SLP2 expression in hippocampal neurons (HNs) from the treated group, along with the enrichment of mitophagy-related pathways. Functional experiments confirmed that SLP2 regulates the PINK1/Parkin pathway, promotes mitophagy, and maintains neuronal energy homeostasis. Conversely, knockdown of SLP2 reversed the antidepressant and neuroprotective effects of UB. Conclusion UB alleviates CUMS-induced depressive-like behavior and hippocampal neuronal damage by upregulating SLP2 and regulating the PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy pathway. This study presents a new potential target and theoretical basis for developing natural compound-based therapies for depression.
authors: Chen F, Tang L, Yuan L, Xiong J, Kuang R, Qian W, Kong Y, Yin Y.
screening_reason: Investigates attenuation of neuroinflammation and hippocampal neuronal damage in a model of depression.
summary_ja: 慢性予測不能軽度ストレス（CUMS）うつ病モデルラットを用いて、天然エラジタンニン由来代謝産物であるウロリチンB（UB）の抗うつ効果を検証した。UB投与により行動異常が改善し、海馬の神経損傷、シナプス消失、および神経炎症が軽減した。単一細胞RNAシーケンシング等の解析により、UBが海馬神経細胞のSLP2発現を高め、PINK1/Parkin経路を介したマイトファジーを促進することが判明した。
summary_en: This study evaluated the effects of urolithin B (UB) in a chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) rat model of depression. UB administration reduced depressive-like behavior, hippocampal neuronal damage, synaptic loss, and neuroinflammation. Mechanistically, UB upregulated SLP2 in hippocampal neurons to activate PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy and preserve neuronal energy homeostasis.
key_finding_ja: ウロリチンBはSLP2発現を高めてPINK1/Parkin経路によるマイトファジーを活性化し、モデルラットのうつ様行動と海馬神経損傷を軽減する。
why_it_matters_ja: うつ病における神経保護・抗炎症効果をもたらす新たな分子標的としてSLP2を介したマイトファジー経路の有用性が示唆される。

title: PlantPTM: A deep learning framework integrating protein language models with multi-view features for predicting diverse post-translational modification sites in plants.
abstract: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) play crucial regulatory roles in plants, orchestrating protein functions to maintain metabolic homeostasis, enable adaptation to dynamic environments, and regulate diverse cellular processes. Thus, the identification of PTM sites is essential for elucidating the mechanisms underlying plant growth, development, and stress responses. However, reliable and cost-effective computational approaches for predicting PTM sites in plants remain lacking. Here, we present PlantPTM, an integrated deep learning framework for predicting nine PTM types in plants. By combining protein language models (PLMs) with evolutionary information, PlantPTM demonstrates robust generalizability across a wide range of PTM types and plant species. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance, with a mean AUROC of 0.8640 and a peak AUROC of 0.9699 across the nine PTM types. Notably, PlantPTM maintains strong performance even under low-data scenarios and unseen species. Extensive comparative benchmarks demonstrate that PlantPTM outperforms existing PTM prediction tools by an average of 15.46%, with improvements ranging from 2.90% to 19.08% over the best-performing tools for each PTM type. Furthermore, independent in-house MS data confirmed the accuracy of PlantPTM for ubiquitination, acetylation, and N-glycosylation sites, with all AUROC values exceeding 0.8. To facilitate PTM studies in plants, we provide the PlantPTM online service and source code freely available at https://ai4bio.online/PlantPTM and https://github.com/wky0422/PlantPTM, respectively.
authors: Dou G, Wang K, Qin Z, Zhang M, Zhang W, Miao C, Li J, Chen Z.
screening_reason: Presents a deep learning framework dedicated to identifying and predicting diverse protein post-translational modification sites.
summary_ja: 植物における翻訳後修飾（PTM）部位の同定は、機能解析や環境適応機構の解明に不可欠ですが、高精度な計算予測手法が不十分でした。本研究では、タンパク質言語モデル（PLM）と進化的特徴を統合したディープラーニングフレームワーク「PlantPTM」を開発しました。PlantPTMは9種類のPTM（ユビキチン化、アセチル化、N-配糖化など）の予測において平均AUROC 0.8640を達成し、既存ツールを平均15.46%上回る性能を示しました。データ量が少ない場合や未学習の種においても高い汎化性能を維持することが確認されています。
summary_en: PlantPTM, a deep learning framework integrating protein language models with multi-view features, was developed to predict nine types of protein post-translational modifications in plants. It demonstrated superior performance across diverse plant species with a mean AUROC of 0.8640, outperforming existing computational tools. Independent mass spectrometry datasets validated its high prediction accuracy for ubiquitination, acetylation, and N-glycosylation.
key_finding_ja: タンパク質言語モデルを活用した「PlantPTM」の開発により、植物における9種類の翻訳後修飾部位を高精度かつ汎用的に予測することが可能になった。
why_it_matters_ja: 植物の多様な翻訳後修飾を計算科学的に高精度予測できるプラットフォームは、植物の成長やストレス応答研究の加速に貢献することが期待されます。

title: Neuroinflammatory pathways linking pain and rehabilitation outcomes in schizophrenia: a narrative review.
abstract: Introduction Schizophrenia is a chronic and disabling neuropsychiatric disorder traditionally defined by psychotic and cognitive symptoms. Increasing evidence suggests that neuroinflammatory mechanisms contribute to its pathophysiology and may also underlie common but underrecognized somatic manifestations. These include altered pain perception, characterized by both diminished sensitivity and chronic pain, with important implications for functional outcomes and rehabilitation. Areas covered This narrative review examines clinical, preclinical, and translational studies addressing the role of neuroinflammation in schizophrenia, with a specific focus on microglial and astrocytic activation, cytokine signaling, oxidative stress pathways, and their interactions with central pain processing circuits. The review was informed by targeted searches of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, covering articles published from database inception to January 2026, with emphasis on studies relevant to pain modulation, symptom expression, and neurobiological heterogeneity in schizophrenia. Expert opinion Neuroinflammation represents a biologically plausible link between core schizophrenia pathology and altered pain perception. Recognition of pain as an integrated component of disease biology, rather than a secondary complaint, may improve clinical assessment and treatment planning. Investigating and targeting neuroinflammatory pathways holds promise for personalized interventions that address neuropsychiatric symptoms and pain, potentially enhancing rehabilitation outcomes and quality of life.
authors: Sedghi Esfahani S, Mahdinia E, Dehkhodaei S, Abedi Oumali N, Taherkhani S, Rafaiee R.
screening_reason: Reviews neuroinflammatory mechanisms, microglial/astrocytic activation, and central neuro-immune interactions affecting pain in schizophrenia.
summary_ja: 統合失調症は精神病症状だけでなく、痛み感覚の低下や慢性痛といった体性症状も伴う障害である。本ナラティブレビューでは、ミクログリアやアストロサイトの活性化、サイトカインシグナル、酸化ストレスなどの神経炎症経路と中枢性痛覚処理回路との相互作用を考察した。文献検索に基づき、神経炎症が痛みの変容や統合失調症の異質性に及ぼす影響を分析した。神経炎症経路の解明は、個別化された治療アプローチやリハビリテーション成果の改善につながる可能性がある。
summary_en: This narrative review addresses the role of neuroinflammation in linking schizophrenia pathophysiology with altered pain perception and functional outcomes. It synthesizes evidence on microglial and astrocytic activation, cytokine signaling, and oxidative stress interacting with central pain circuits in schizophrenia. The findings highlight neuroinflammation as a potential therapeutic target to optimize pain management and rehabilitation outcomes in this population.
key_finding_ja: 統合失調症における痛みの感受性変化とリハビリテーション成果には、ミクログリアやアストロサイトを介した神経炎症経路が関与している可能性が示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 痛みを統合失調症の病態の一部として評価し神経炎症を標的とすることで、臨床評価の向上や効果的なリハビリテーション介入の開発につながる可能性がある。

title: Multidisciplinary Delphi consensus statement on minimal standards for clinical metadata and end points in microbiome studies.
abstract: The lack of harmonization for microbiome-based clinical studies represents a critical issue for microbiome researchers and stakeholders, although microbiome research and clinical studies on the gut microbiome have been intensively conducted for more than a decade. The selection of a minimum metadata set to be analysed and reported during clinical studies with microbiome outcomes, the identification of reference materials, the definition of standardized sampling procedures and data analysis protocols, and the choice of unified clinical end points are still lacking. The two-round Delphi survey, conducted within the framework of the Horizon Europe Human Microbiome Action (HMA) consortium, aimed to standardize metadata collection, sampling procedures, data generation and sharing, and standard operating procedures for aspects of gut microbiome-based clinical studies beyond outcomes. The process involved 72 scientists and experts worldwide in the first round and 61 experts in the second round, with an 85% participation rate from the first to the second round. On the basis of the outcome of the Delphi survey, the HMA consortium provided 15 recommendations that might be taken up by the community at large to promote coherence and harmonization in the way microbiome clinical research is and will be performed. The recommendations mainly focus on the gut microbiome and diseases associated with the gastrointestinal tract and gut-organ axes.
authors: Schierwagen R, Carraturo F, Iyappan A, Brol MJ, Druart C, Israelsen M, Hassani Z, Legent K, Godoy Y, Vecchi C, Rodriguez J, Villesen IF, Jarde A, Arumugam M, Krag A, Maguin E, Bork P, Human Microbiome Action Consortium, Doré J, Trebicka J, Fasano A.
screening_reason: Establishes standardized consensus recommendations for metadata collection and clinical parameters in gut microbiome studies.
summary_ja: 腸内細菌叢に関する臨床研究では、メタデータの選択やサンプリング手順、臨床エンドポイントの統一性が世界的に不足している。本研究ではHorizon Europe Human Microbiome Actionコンソーシアム主導のもと、2ラウンドのデルファイ調査を実施した。国際的な専門家グループが参加し、臨床メタデータやデータ共有の標準化について合意形成を行った。その結果、腸内細菌叢関連の臨床研究における整合性と標準化を推進するための15の推奨事項が取りまとめられた。
summary_en: To address the lack of standardization in clinical microbiome studies, the Horizon Europe Human Microbiome Action consortium conducted a two-round Delphi survey involving international experts. The process achieved high expert participation to harmonize clinical metadata collection, sampling, data analysis, and clinical end points. Consequently, 15 recommendations were formulated to promote standardized and reproducible gut microbiome clinical research.
key_finding_ja: デルファイ調査を通じて、腸内細菌叢に関する臨床研究のメタデータ収集およびデータ生成の標準化に向けた15の推奨事項が策定された。
why_it_matters_ja: 共通の標準化指針が導入されることで、異なる臨床研究間のデータの比較可能性や統合解析の精度向上につながることが期待される。

title: Honokiol alleviates oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and apoptosis in excitotoxicity induced by ouabain, a Na + /K + -ATPase inhibitor.
abstract: Excitotoxicity, oxidative stress, and neuroinflammation play significant roles in the pathophysiology of neurodegenerative disorders. This study aims to examine the impact of honokiol (HNK) on antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-apoptotic mechanisms in a model of excitotoxicity induced by intracerebroventricular (icv) ouabain (OUA) in rats. Rats were allocated to five equal groups (n = 10): (I) Animals given intraperitoneal isotonic saline solution for seven days (Control); (II) animals given a single dose of 5 μl OUA solvent (artificial cerebrospinal fluid-icv) on the first day (Sham); (III) animals given a single dose of OUA (5 μl at a concentration of 10⁻³ M-icv) (OUA); (IV) Animals given HNK for seven days (HNK); (V) animals given OUA and then HNK for seven days (OUA+HNK). OUA administration caused an increase in cerebral cortex malondialdehyde (MDA) and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) levels and a decrease in glutathione (GSH) and superoxide dismutase (SOD) levels. The OUA injection resulted in a decrease in immobility in the forced swim test, an increase in swimming and climbing activities, and a decrease in Na + /K + -ATPase enzyme activity. Significant improvements in oxidative stress markers and tissue antioxidant levels were detected with HNK treatment. Additionally, HNK treatment inhibited apoptotic processes by increasing Heat Shock Protein-70 (HSP-70) and suppressing the expression of the pro-apoptotic protein Bax. Furthermore, histopathological changes caused by OUA administration were found to improve in the HNK-treated groups. In conclusion, our findings suggest that HNK therapy, by reducing oxidative tissue damage, apoptosis, and inflammation, may be a promising adjunctive treatment for pathologies presenting with excitotoxicity.
authors: Demir M, Basak F, Kusat T, Weli SHW.
screening_reason: Studies the protective effects of honokiol against neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and excitotoxicity in the brain.
summary_ja: 本研究では、ウアバイン（OUA）の脳室内投与により誘発された興奮毒性ラットモデルにおいて、ホノキオール（HNK）の抗酸化・抗炎症・抗アポトーシス作用を評価した。OUA投与は脳皮質のMDAおよびTNF-αの上昇、GSHおよびSODの低下、Na+/K+-ATPase活性の低下を引き起こした。これに対し、HNK処理は酸化ストレス指標および組織抗酸化レベルを顕著に改善させた。さらにHNKはHSP-70の増加とBaxの抑制を介してアポトーシスを抑制し、組織病理学的変化を軽快させた。
summary_en: This study evaluated the effects of honokiol (HNK) on oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and apoptosis in a rat model of excitotoxicity induced by intracerebroventricular ouabain (OUA) administration. OUA administration increased cortical MDA and TNF-alpha levels, decreased GSH and SOD levels, and reduced Na+/K+-ATPase activity. HNK treatment significantly improved oxidative stress markers and antioxidant levels, inhibited apoptotic pathways by increasing HSP-70 and suppressing Bax expression, and attenuated histopathological damage.
key_finding_ja: ホノキオール投与はウアバイン誘発興奮毒性モデルラットにおいて、酸化ストレス、神経炎症、およびアポトーシスの抑制を介して組織障害を軽減した。
why_it_matters_ja: 興奮毒性が関与する神経変性疾患において、ホノキオールが保護的な補助療法として有効である可能性が示唆される。

title: Ethanol exposure suppresses Microglia pro-inflammatory response induced by SARS-CoV2-Spike protein.
abstract: Background In the central nervous system (CNS), microglial cells regulate the immune response by mediating neuroinflammation. Alcohol abuse leads to neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration in CNS. In the context of COVID-19, neuroinflammation and glial reactivity are mediated by the infection of human glial cells by SARS-CoV-2, which recognizes the angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) and other proteins, such as transmembrane serine protease 2 (TMPRSS2), through its surface Spike-1 protein. Although several risk factors for COVID-19 progression have been described, it remains unknown how alcohol consumption affects SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein-induced microglial reactivity. In this study, murine microglial cultures (BV-2) were exposed to ethanol alone and subsequently challenged with the Spike protein. Immunofluorescence analysis revealed that ethanol treatment (1%) did not affect the levels of the reactivity-related proteins C3 and CD86 or the phagocytic potential of microglial cells, although it reduced the number of cells exhibiting an amoeboid morphology. However, ethanol treatment prevented the Spike protein-induced increase in C3 levels, amoeboid cell numbers, and phagocytic activity. Furthermore, chronic in vivo exposure to ethanol decreased ACE2 and TMPRSS2 levels in the cerebral cortex of mice, whereas treatment with higher ethanol concentrations in vitro decreased only TMPRSS2 levels. These data suggest that ethanol exposure suppresses the ability of microglia to respond to the pro-inflammatory effects induced by the Spike protein. This impairment may contribute to the loss of microglial function in regulating the immune response and neuroinflammation in the CNS in the context of COVID-19.
authors: Esteves B, Nascimento LAHD, Stipursky J.
screening_reason: Investigates how ethanol modulates microglial pro-inflammatory activation and neuroinflammation induced by SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein.
summary_ja: COVID-19における中枢神経系の免疫応答に対するアルコール曝露の影響を解明するため、マウスミクログリア培養系（BV-2）と生体モデルを用いて検討が行われた。エタノール単独処理はミクログリアの基本的な食作用や特定マーカーのレベルを変えなかったが、アメーバ様形態への変化を減少させた。さらに、エタノール処理はSARS-CoV-2 Spikeタンパク質によって誘導されるC3発現上昇、形態変化、および食作用の亢進を抑制した。マウス大脳皮質における慢性エタノール曝露はウイルス受容体であるACE2およびTMPRSS2の発現低下を引き起こすことも確認された。
summary_en: The study evaluated how ethanol exposure modulates SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein-induced microglial activation in vitro and in vivo. Pre-treatment with ethanol suppressed Spike protein-induced microglial reactivity, preventing increases in C3 levels, morphologic transition to an amoeboid state, and heightened phagocytic activity. Furthermore, chronic ethanol exposure reduced the expression of key viral entry proteins ACE2 and TMPRSS2 in the mouse cerebral cortex.
key_finding_ja: エタノール曝露は、SARS-CoV-2 Spikeタンパク質によって引き起こされるミクログリアの炎症性応答および形態的変化を抑制する。
why_it_matters_ja: アルコール摂取が感染刺激に対するミクログリアの正常な免疫応答機能を減弱させ、中枢神経系における神経炎症調節の低下につながる可能性が示唆される。

title: Intranasal Administration of Isoeugenol Improves Memory Deficits in APP/PS1 Old Mice-A Role Beyond Nrf2 Activation?
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD), a neurodegenerative disorder and the most common cause of dementia, has no cure or effective treatment; thus, identification of disease-modifying therapeutics is crucial. Nrf2 is a master controller of homeostatic functions whose activity is compromised in AD. Most pharmacological Nrf2 activators are electrophilic molecules that covalently modify cysteine residues in the thiol-rich Keap1, and many are Michael acceptors, such as low-molecular-weight (LMW) skin allergens. However, LMW allergens-induced Nrf2 activation in a pharmacological setting has only recently attracted attention, exemplified by the clinical success of Dimethyl Fumarate. Hence, we investigated, for the first time, the potential of the skin allergen Isoeugenol to activate Nrf2 and reverse selected AD hallmarks, both in vitro and in vivo, in AD-specific models. In vitro studies were performed using microglia cells exposed to LPS and neuronal cells overexpressing human APP with Swedish mutation, to evaluate Isoeugenol's potential in decreasing neuroinflammation and activating the Nrf2 pathway, respectively. In vivo studies were conducted in 10-month-old AD double-transgenic mice (APP/PS1), which were intranasally administered Isougenol. Isoeugenol's pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic profile, and its effect on mice cognition were evaluated. The results showed that Isoeugenol (1) activated Nrf2 in AD neuronal cells (likely involving AKT signaling); (2) exhibited antioxidant and Nrf2-dependent anti-inflammatory activity, which was abolished after Nrf2 silencing; (3) exhibited good pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic profiles; (4) reduced the levels of Aβ peptides in vitro and in vivo; (5) reduced triglyceride and LDL cholesterol levels in treated mice; and (6) improved the memory deficits in old mice. This is the first study reporting Isoeugenol's intranasal administration, and on specific AD mice models. Overall, the results reinforce Isoeugenol as a pleiotropic molecule, with great potential for AD treatment.
authors: Silva A, Silva S, Macedo J, Moreira P, Baptista D, Bicker J, Fortuna A, Liberal J, Rodrigues B, Resende R, Vitorino I, Santos AE, Neves BM, Pereira C, Cruz MT.
journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
screening_reason: Evaluates Isoeugenol's ability to attenuate microglial neuroinflammation and cognitive deficits in Alzheimer's disease models.
summary_ja: 本研究では、皮膚アレルゲンであるイソオイゲノールのNrf2活性化作用およびアルツハイマー病（AD）病態に対する改善効果をインビトロおよびインビボのADモデルで検証した。インビトロにおいて、イソオイゲノールはNrf2を活性化し、Nrf2依存的な抗炎症作用およびAβペプチドの減少をもたらした。10か月齢のAPP/PS1マウスへの経鼻投与では、Aβペプチドや脂質レベルが低下し、記憶障害の改善が観察された。
summary_en: This study investigated the potential of the skin allergen isoeugenol to activate Nrf2 and attenuate Alzheimer's disease (AD) hallmarks in vitro and in vivo. In cell models, isoeugenol activated Nrf2 signaling and exerted Nrf2-dependent anti-inflammatory effects while reducing A-beta peptides. Intranasal administration of isoeugenol to 10-month-old APP/PS1 mice reduced A-beta and lipid levels, and significantly improved memory deficits.
key_finding_ja: イソオイゲノールの経鼻投与は、APP/PS1マウスモデルにおいてNrf2経路の活性化や抗炎症作用を伴い記憶障害を改善した。
why_it_matters_ja: イソオイゲノールのような多面的作用を持つ低分子化合物が、アルツハイマー病に対する新たな治療法として応用できる可能性がある。

title: Effects of diarrhea and antibiotic-induced microbial elimination on dynamic changes in fecal microbial communities and antibiotic resistance of Hu sheep lambs ( Ovis aries ).
abstract: Background As a highly reproductive meat sheep breed in China, Hu sheep is an important economic group in ruminant animal breeding. However, research on its intestinal microbiomes under the background of diarrhea and antibiotic treatment remains relatively limited. Methods This study investigated the intestinal microbiota of Hu sheep lambs in the preliminary stage of diarrhea (group DM), the late recovery stage of diarrhea (group DL), and the healthy stage (group H). Diseased individuals (groups DM and DL) were treated with a combination of Shuanghuanglian, Cefazolin, Lincomycin, and Dexamethasone (0.2 mL dosage). To characterize the intestinal microbiota, fecal samples were collected from all groups, and metagenomic sequencing was performed. Using metagenomic binning tools and co-assembly methods, we reconstructed 482 high-quality non-redundant metagenome assembled genomes (MAGs). Results Among these MAGs, 70% belong to the phyla Bacillota, Bacteroidota, and Pseudomonadota, highly consistent with the typical structure of intestinal microbiota in ruminants. Functional annotation revealed that the genes encoding carbohydrate-active enzymes (CAZymes) are more abundant in Bacillota and Bacteroidota, which supports the degradation and energy metabolism functions of Hu sheep on fibrous feed. During the preliminary stage of diarrhea, the virulence genes carried by symbiotic bacteria such as Lachnospiraceae, Acutalibacteraceae and Bacteroidaceae were enriched. Although diarrhea symptoms alleviated during the late recovery stage of diarrhea, the combined use of multiple antibiotics led to the continuous enrichment of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) related to lincosamides and cephalosporins. The average abundance of cephalosporin-related ARGs in group DL was significantly higher than that in group DM and H, indicating a risk of residual ARGs. Microbial diversity analysis showed that there was no significant overall difference in MAGs between group DM and H, but both groups showed significant differences compared to group DL, suggesting that antibiotic driven clearance of sensitive bacteria is the core driving force. Moreover, our study shows that the abundance of the zoonotic pathogens Barnesiella and Campylobacter significantly increased in the diarrhea group ( p Conclusions This study not only expands the genomic database of ruminant intestinal microorganisms but also provides a key theoretical basis for formulating intestinal microecological regulation strategies and optimizing diarrhea treatment regimens for Hu sheep.
authors: Li X, Jiang J, Li X, Jian G, Li F.
screening_reason: Analyzes the composition and metabolic resistance profiles of the lamb intestinal microbiota during diarrhea and antibiotic administration.
